story.value: Terbium was discovered in 1843 by Carl-Gustav Mosander, a Swedish surgeon and chemist.
The name terbium comes from the village of Ytterby in Sweden.
The names first given to the erbium and terbium samples have since been switched.

uses.value: Terbium is used to dope some types of solid-state devices.
Terbium is used with zirconium dioxide as a crystal stabilizer in fuel cells that operate at high temperatures.
A terbium compound called sodium terbium borate is used to make laser light.
Terbium oxide could potentially be used as an activator for green phosphors in television tubes.
